claims.claim_ar: الهمزة (أَمْ) هنا تستخدم استفهاماً إنكارياً لرفض الزعم وإظهار استنكاره؛ أي أسلوب استنكاري ترويجي للدحض.
claims.claim_en: The hamza interrogative 'أَمْ' functions as an accusatory/denying rhetorical question, rejecting the claim and highlighting its implausibility (rhetorical interrogation for repudiation).
claims.rhetorical_effect: Expresses strong reproach and forces the hearer to reconsider the absurdity of the allegation (heightens the tone of refutation).

claims.source_quote_ar: (وَما كانَ هذَا الْقُرْآنُ أَنْ يُفْتَرى مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ)
claims.claim_ar: المفردة (تَفْتَرُونَ) تندرج في سياق نفي الاتهام بالافتراء على الله؛ أسلوب بلاغي يلتمس دحض تهمة كون الوحي مُفتَرى.
claims.claim_en: The verb 'تَفْتَرُونَ' is part of a rhetorical refutation of the accusation that the revelation is fabricated; it invokes the motif of 'افتراء' (fabrication) to deny and condemn the claim.
claims.needs_review_reason: Source chunk cites the theme of 'افتراء' and its refutation in commentary on related verses; the exact lexical and contextual match to this specific ayah is inferred from that commentary rather than quoted verbatim from the same verse.
claims.rhetorical_effect: Frames the opponents' claim as a serious falsehood (fabrication), thereby morally discrediting them and strengthening the Prophet's credibility.

warnings: Provided source_chunks are primarily iʿrāb/tafsir excerpts (Darwish, Zamakhshari, Safi) rather than the specific authors requested (al-Jurjani, al-Sakkaki, al-Baqillani, al-Suyuti, tafsir balagha). Claims were extracted only where an exact substring match to the provided chunks exists.
